description: Grainger is an industrial-supply distribution company, focused on safety, security, and storage equipment, along with cleaning, metalworking, and hand tools. As of 2025, it offers over 30 million products to some 4.5 million customers worldwide, but its services are primarily in North America, Japan, and the United Kingdom. The company was founded in 1927.

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Chicago
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

"Grainger actually works and lives by our principles: Start with the customer, embrace curiosity, act with intent, compete with urgency, win as one team, invest in our success and do the right thing.  They come together to support one another, even those we've never met.  I've loved working for this company for over 16 years and hope to remain with the company throughout my professional career."

"Our CEO not only lives our core principles but ensures that we hold strong to those principles no matter the political or economic climate. I have worked for corporate companies prior to Grainger, and the overall feeling of connectiveness to each other, to community, and to self, is one that I had not experienced prior. I feel at home with Grainger."

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Grainger is the country’s leading distributor of maintenance, repair, and supplies for industries like hardware, lighting, and plumbing. Established in 1927, the company now operates the 11th largest online e-commerce site by revenue.
 

Grainger is building two new distribution centers in the U.S., and is adding 3.5 million square feet to its supply chain network for a more than 35% increase in overall warehouse space.
 

In 2022, the company trained all of its team members in a DEI learning course, focusing on unconscious bias and how it emerges in day-to-day work. It aims to have half of its senior leadership roles filled by women by 2030. Currently, its CEO’s leadership team is 43% women while 29% is racially diverse.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
This long-standing industrial supply company is adapting to the changing times with an emphasis on diversity.

  • In the last year, Grainger implemented a technology tool to remove noninclusive language from over 400 job postings; after the revisions went live, the pool of female applicants increased by 15%.

  • A mandatory e-learning course for leaders tackles unconscious bias, including how it may emerge in day-to-day work and behaviors for managing it.

  • Senior leadership values transparency, holding monthly calls with all employees to address questions ranging from business operations questions to U.S. Supreme Court decisions to employee compensation.

  • “Every team member I have encountered during my time at Grainger so far is caring and willing to help each individual succeed,” said one worker. “You are welcomed with open arms, work together as one team, and [colleagues are] willing to help you develop professionally and personally.”

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: This industrial supplies company has appeared on the Best Companies list five times thanks to its emphasis on employee training and its focus on corporate inclusivity. From each team member’s first day, Grainger offers a variety of professional learning opportunities, skills training courses, and leadership programs. Employees spent an average of six hours last year on these supplemental trainings. “I feel that the company never lacks development opportunities,” says one staffer. “It is a main focus of every manager I have worked with so far, having been offered the opportunity to participate in classes and get involved with projects that align to my interests.” Additionally, the company is invested in its diversity efforts, conducting pay equity audits each year and aiming for 50% of its leadership team to be women by 2030.
